purpose_of_this_fixture: Calibration fixture for the cue-export shred case (REAL-CALL-LESSONS C58c; BUILD-PLAN 4.2 row s16). A discovery call with a sign fabrication company, exported as WebVTT with individually timed units carrying start and end times. The export is dishonestly clean: it marks nothing, yet it wedges one-word units of one speaker inside another speaker's run at zero-millisecond gaps, re-emits the last words of a unit as the first words of the next, truncates one figure mid-word, labels one speaker with a bare initial whose spoken name never appears in a label, and carries one name-shaped unit that matches nobody. Roughly two fifths of adjacent units share a label. The key asserts the repair, not only the reading: every wedge is flagged and never absorbed into the run around it, boundary duplication is recorded and removed only outside quotation marks, the initial-only label resolves by adjacency pair and by nothing else, the stray name is name-shaped noise that creates no person, a quote spanning same-speaker units is a merged run cited as 'cues N-M', and a quote whose span crosses another speaker's label is refused. It guards reversal R2: the citation contract's safety clause is the speaker boundary, not the turn boundary, so a grader that reinstates the turn-boundary clause fails here because almost nothing in this file would be quotable. Beside the intake assertions the 25 fields grade the call itself: Discovery complete with R4 met-with-residual, R5 not-obtainable from this room, R11 missing and R12 partial, two excavated pains, a Work Management build for jobs, permits and the shop screen with quotes on native CRM boards third in the client's own order.
transcript_format: WebVTT export with the speaker label inside the cue payload: a 'WEBVTT' header line, then numbered cues 1 to 298, each with a timing line 'HH:MM:SS.mmm --> HH:MM:SS.mmm' and one text line 'Label: text'. No participant header and no call date. Four labels: 'Consultant', 'Rosamund Achterberg', 'Nkechi Brandvold' and the bare initial 'R', whose spoken name (Ruairi) never appears in a label. Cues run from 00:00:02.045 to 00:22:45.303 with about 3,173 spoken words. Timestamps are zero-padded, millisecond, strictly monotonic, with no collisions and no overlaps; the units are short (longest 37 words, 12.8 seconds, cue 177), so no composite block is structurally possible. 121 of the 297 adjacent pairs share a label (40.7 percent); 33 units begin lowercase and 34 lack terminal punctuation once bracketed tokens are stripped, because a sentence routinely spans two to four units of one speaker. Nine wedges sit at zero-millisecond gaps on both sides (cues 70, 86, 97, 119, 132, 136, 165, 270, 272). Seven boundary duplications or truncations: cues 29/30 'square-foot plant', 76/77 'on the', 102/103 'por' then 'portal', 114/115 'are the', 185/186 'thirteen thou' then 'thirteen thousand', 210/211 'four', and 164/166 'the paint booth had' across the wedge at 165. Two recognition errors: cue 258 'science' for 'signs', in no name, product, status or column slot, and cue 264 'Bow' for 'Bao', an absent person's name that resolves to the designer introduced whole at cue 55. Cue 72 is the one-word unit 'Corwin.' One unlabelled pause of 5.8 seconds before cue 179; total unlabelled silence 159.5 seconds, 11.7 percent of the span. Client share about 75 percent by words and by speaking seconds (Rosamund 41, Ruairi 17, Nkechi 17 by words); the longest own-side stretch is 64 words over cues 21 to 23. Bracketed cues: [laughs], [sighs]. ASCII only. Two location forms, both taken from the transcript's own numbering: a single cue is 'cue N, HH:MM:SS.mmm, Label' with the label exactly as printed (so 'R' for the initial-only speaker); a merged same-speaker run is 'cues N-M, HH:MM:SS.mmm, Label' with the start time of cue N, and its quote is the cue texts of N to M joined by one space, boundary duplication kept inside the marks. No location in this key crosses a label change.

company.name: Tallgrass Sign and Display
company.industry: Full-service sign fabrication and installation: channel letters, monument signs, wayfinding for hospitals and campuses, a little vehicle graphics. Customers are retail landlords, general contractors, tenants and, for the largest current contract, a hospital system.
company.size: About forty-eight people: twenty-two in the shop, three install crews (nine on the road), and an office of design, estimating, the general manager, the coordinator and the estimator. The founder is 'here every day and also retired'.
company.locations: One plant of about thirty thousand square feet, started in a two-bay garage in the eighties, serving about two hundred miles of territory. City, county and suburban permit offices each behave differently.
current_tools: The estimator's quoting spreadsheet: one file, about nine years old, thirty-four tabs, about sixty open quotes at a time. Each quote goes out by email and is not chased
The accounting system: a job number carrying only the customer and the amount
A shared drive: a job folder per job for everything else, including a weekly photo of the whiteboard
The production whiteboard: the back wall of the shop office, a magnet per job, stations as columns (router, paint, letters, wiring, crating, install), moved by hand every morning
The coordinator's permit spreadsheet (job number, city, dates, expiry). Expiry reminders she sets by hand on her calendar. The city's permit portal, checked by hand
A rented crane from one outfit; when they are booked the company is booked
No monday account of any kind ('That's the extent of it.'); an industry-specific package was demoed two years ago and set aside

Backcharges, crane fees and re-permit fees: named and unquantified, Missing. Weakest element reported, and the whole is Met-with-residual: the client's own total 'sixty to seventy thousand a year' stands, and the residual becomes one gap question (pull the actual remake and backcharge figures).
